notes: Delete mirror of finance-replace-0008: removes the original rule; members reached only through it lose their answer. Re-picked by the verifier for variety: the scouted pair of price-effect rules (substitutes 0006, complements 0008) were near mirrors, and both rest on definitions whose by-name worlds are strained. Here the class is an index whose membership is contingent (reviewed every quarter), and a member's listing makes sense without it, so the by-name world (the company leaves the CAC 40 and stays listed in Paris) is natural. R1: the index's selection rule draws only from companies listed on Euronext Paris, so the rule has no exception; LVMH and BNP Paribas have no other exchange listing (only over-the-counter ADRs), so their answers are single. In a by-name world the member's stored listing wins and its index membership gives way; it never stays in the CAC 40 as an exception (README Decisions 2). Lopsided: both are among the index's largest members. Derivability very_unlikely: stated directly. Plausibility: Paris and London are Europe's two main exchanges, and French groups have weighed London or New York listings, so London is plausible and clearly false. 'Listed on' has cardinality many; the new-member prompts give no other route to an exchange. The near query asks the DAX's country, whose answer is not the edit's new value.
